title: ALIGNAgent: Adaptive Learner Intelligence for Gap Identification and Next-step guidance
extended_summary:
This paper addresses the problem that many personalized learning systems in education handle only one part of the adaptive learning process, such as knowledge tracing, diagnostic modeling, or recommendation, rather than integrating them into a complete cycle. The authors argue that this fragmentation prevents timely, targeted support for students who move on to new topics with unresolved misconceptions. Their research question is whether a coordinated multi-agent framework can use authentic course data to estimate knowledge proficiency, identify concept-level skill gaps, and recommend next-step resources in a way that aligns with actual student performance.

The proposed intervention is ALIGNAgent, a multi-agent framework composed primarily of a Skill Gap Agent, a Recommender Agent, and a Summary Agent. The system processes learner preferences, gradebook records, and quiz/question-level performance data to estimate topic proficiency, detect specific conceptual weaknesses, and retrieve preference-aware resources such as videos, tutorials, and readings. It also generates narrative feedback summarizing strengths, weaknesses, and recommended actions. The framework was evaluated using multiple large language models, with GPT-4o, Claude 3.5 Sonnet, and Llama 3 included in experiments; GPT-4o-based agents showed the strongest performance.

The population studied was undergraduate students in two computer science courses at Florida Polytechnic University in the United States: COP 3415 (Data Structures, 14 students) and CDA 2108 (Fundamentals of Computer Systems, 11 students), both offered in Summer 2025. The setting was a classroom course context using authentic course assessments, gradebooks, and a learning-preferences survey. Midterm and final exam performance served as ground truth for validation, while quiz performance and preferences were used as inputs to the system.

The main conclusions are that ALIGNAgent can effectively integrate proficiency estimation, skill-gap identification, and personalized resource recommendation using real educational data, and that GPT-4o was the strongest model for question-difficulty labeling and downstream proficiency estimation. The paper reports that GPT-4o-based agents achieved precision of 0.87-0.90 and F1 scores of 0.84-0.87 in knowledge proficiency estimation when validated against actual exam performance. Overall, the authors conclude that a multi-agent AI pipeline can provide interpretable, targeted learner support in higher education, though the study is based on a small sample from a single institution.

identified_tools.name: ALIGNAgent
identified_tools.description: A proposed multi-agent personalized learning framework that integrates knowledge proficiency estimation, concept-level skill-gap identification, and preference-aware learning resource recommendation using LLM-based agents.
identified_tools.use_case: Studied as an adaptive higher-education learning system using quiz, gradebook, and learner preference data from two undergraduate computer science courses to estimate topic proficiency, identify skill gaps, and recommend targeted resources; GPT-4o-, Claude-, and LLaMA-based agents were compared for labeling and proficiency estimation performance.

findings.finding_summary: On authentic datasets from two undergraduate computer science courses, ALIGNAgent with GPT-4o-based agents achieved precision of 0.87-0.90 and F1 scores of 0.84-0.87 in knowledge proficiency estimation when validated against actual exam performance. The paper describes this as evidence of effectiveness for proficiency estimation, but does not report effect sizes, confidence intervals, or a total combined sample beyond course enrollments.
findings.measure: Knowledge proficiency estimation performance validated against actual exam performance (precision, F1)

findings.finding_summary: For question difficulty labeling, GPT-4o-based ALIGNAgent components outperformed other labeling approaches on COP3415 and CDA2108. In COP3415, GPT-4o achieved precision=0.81, recall=0.53, F1=0.61, accuracy=0.52; in CDA2108, it achieved precision=0.88, recall=0.61, F1=0.72, accuracy=0.63.
findings.measure: Question difficulty labeling performance (precision, recall, F1, accuracy)

identified_tools.name: ChatGPT
identified_tools.description: OpenAI GPT-family large language model used here as an LLM agent for educational question difficulty labeling and learner knowledge/proficiency estimation.
identified_tools.use_case: GPT-4o was used as the LLM backbone in agent configurations to label question difficulty and estimate student knowledge proficiency/skill gaps within the ALIGNAgent framework.

findings.finding_summary: For question labeling against instructor references, ChatGPT (GPT-4o) had the strongest reported performance across both datasets. In COP3415 it achieved precision=0.81, recall=0.53, F1=0.61, accuracy=0.52; in CDA2108 it achieved precision=0.88, recall=0.61, F1=0.72, accuracy=0.63.
findings.measure: Question difficulty labeling performance versus instructor labels

findings.finding_summary: GPT-4o-based agents achieved precision of 0.87-0.90 and F1 scores of 0.84-0.87 for knowledge proficiency estimation validated against actual exam performance. The paper reports these results across two undergraduate computer science course datasets, but does not provide confidence intervals or effect sizes.
findings.measure: Knowledge proficiency estimation performance validated against exam outcomes

identified_tools.name: Claude
identified_tools.description: Anthropic Claude-family large language model used here for educational question difficulty labeling within the comparative evaluation.
identified_tools.use_case: Claude 3.5 Sonnet was evaluated as an alternative LLM for automatic question difficulty labeling in the ALIGNAgent experimental setup.

findings.finding_summary: Claude showed lower question-labeling performance than GPT-4o in both datasets. In COP3415, Claude achieved precision=0.72, recall=0.56, F1=0.58, accuracy=0.52; in CDA2108, precision=0.80, recall=0.59, F1=0.68, accuracy=0.60.
findings.measure: Question difficulty labeling performance versus instructor labels

identified_tools.name: LLaMA
identified_tools.description: Meta LLaMA-family large language model used here for educational question difficulty labeling within the comparative evaluation.
identified_tools.use_case: LLaMA 3/3.3 was evaluated as an alternative LLM for automatic question difficulty labeling in the ALIGNAgent experimental setup.

findings.finding_summary: LLaMA's question-labeling performance was below GPT-4o overall, though competitive on some metrics. In COP3415, LLaMA achieved precision=0.82, recall=0.58, F1=0.56, accuracy=0.52; in CDA2108, precision=0.80, recall=0.59, F1=0.68, accuracy=0.60.
findings.measure: Question difficulty labeling performance versus instructor labels

quality_tier_rationale: This is an empirical evaluation on authentic course datasets, but it is not an RCT or strong quasi-experimental design assessing causal effects on student learning. The study mainly reports classification-style performance metrics for proficiency estimation and labeling with a very small sample from two courses.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper reports promising precision and F1 metrics for system performance, but does not provide causal evidence of improvement in student outcomes or standardized effect sizes. Educational impact is therefore positive but unclear in magnitude.
